stated_availability: Data availability statement (p. 10): "The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252." Section 2 (p. 2): "The entire R code (R Core Team, 2024) used for all the analysis and visualizations contained in this paper is at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252 to enable re-use of materials and improve reproducibility and transparency ... All the figures, tables, and statistical test results presented here can be independently reproduced with the code and data in this compendium (Marwick et al., 2018). The R code is released under the MIT license, the data as CC-0, and figures as CC-BY, to enable maximum re-use." Fig. 2 caption (p. 4) points to the same DOI for model specifications and diagnostics.

barriers: Upstream Clarivate Web of Science source database is subscription-only (Tier 2, paywall); the derived 9,697-article analysis dataset is stated to be in the open Zenodo compendium

F1.evidence: Data deposited in a Zenodo research compendium with its own DOI: "openly available in Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252" (Data availability statement, p. 10). The pack resolves this concept DOI at DataCite (state findable) and at Zenodo (current version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15603267).

F2.evidence: The pack shows an independent DataCite metadata record for the deposit (metadata_record true; publisher Zenodo; publication_year 2025; resource_type recorded; title 'benmarwick/web-of-science-archaeology: Research compendium for the publication "Is archaeology a science?"' in the pack's Zenodo search). Platform-table Row 2 also entitles DataCite metadata.

F3.evidence: Pack: identifier_in_metadata true for both the DataCite and Zenodo records of 10.5281/zenodo.14897252. Row 1 also entitles a DataCite record carrying the identifier.

F4.evidence: The DOI is registered and indexed at DataCite with state 'findable' (pack), and hosted on Zenodo, a searchable registry.

A1.evidence: Data-completeness coverage is complete (4/4 required inputs at Tier 0-2). The paper says the full set of inputs is in the compendium: "All the figures, tables, and statistical test results presented here can be independently reproduced with the code and data in this compendium". The compendium can be retrieved over HTTPS by DOI resolution, and the Zenodo access_right is open (pack).

A1_1.evidence: Retrieval is by HTTPS DOI resolution to Zenodo. The record is access_right 'open' (pack), so no proprietary protocol or subscription is needed for the deposited data.

A1_2.evidence: The resource is fully open and needs no authentication ("openly available in Zenodo"; pack access_right open). Under v2.1 a fully open resource satisfies A1.2.

A2.evidence: Zenodo deposit (platform-table Row 2): tombstone page with DOI retained on withdrawal, and metadata always publicly accessible. The pack confirms the deposit is on Zenodo with a DataCite record.

I1.evidence: Neither the paper nor the pack states the file format or structure of the deposited bibliometric data. The paper only says "code and data in this compendium", and the pack records no format field. No platform-table entitlement covers data format, so the ladder is exhausted and the sub-principle is unscoreable, scoring 0.

I2.evidence: Searched the paper and pack for controlled vocabularies or ontologies with PIDs applied to the data (for example, subject schemes or field-level vocabularies). None found. Variables are ad hoc bibliometric measures (number of authors, relative title length, pages, Price index, Shannon diversity).

I3.evidence: Searched for typed, PID-based references in the data's metadata to related resources, such as the Web of Science source or Fanelli and Glänzel (2013). The paper cites Fanelli and Glänzel by DOI in its reference list, but the pack records no related-identifier fields for the deposit, and the WoS source has no PID.

R1.evidence: The paper describes the dataset with many attributes. The sample is 9,697 Archaeology-category 'article' records from 1975-2025, drawn from 28,871 and filtered to 20 journals. The variables are number of authors, relative title length, number of pages, recency of references (Price index), and diversity of references (Shannon index), with modelling families given in the Fig. 2 caption (pp. 2-4).

R1_1.evidence: The paper asserts "the data as CC-0" (p. 2), but the service records cc-by-4.0 for the same deposit (pack licence_conflicts: conflict true). This is a same-artefact disagreement, so the more restrictive CC-BY-4.0 governs. It is a clear, identified licence, so R1.1 is satisfied.

R1_2.evidence: The provenance is documented in detail: "collected from Clarivate's Web of Science database by first selecting the Web of Science category 'Archaeology' and the Document type 'article' (n = 28,871)... filtered the results to keep only articles published in the top 25 journals according to their h-indices as reported by Clarivate's Journal Citation Indicator. Finally, I excluded journals with less than 100 articles" (p. 2). The method follows Fanelli and Glänzel (2013).

R1_3.evidence: Qualifying route (a), a generic metadata schema: the deposit is described by a DataCite metadata record (pack, DataCite endpoint resolved; Zenodo Row 2 entitles DataCite metadata).

F1.evidence: "The entire R code ... used for all the analysis and visualizations contained in this paper is at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252" (p. 2). The concept DOI resolves to version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15603267, resource_type software (pack).

F2.evidence: Independent DataCite/Zenodo metadata record for the software compendium (metadata_record true; resource_type Software; publisher Zenodo; publication_year 2025), titled 'benmarwick/web-of-science-archaeology: Research compendium for the publication "Is archaeology a science?"' (pack).

F3.evidence: Pack: identifier_in_metadata true for both the DataCite and Zenodo records.

F4.evidence: Indexed at DataCite, state 'findable' (pack), and hosted on Zenodo.

A1.evidence: The paper's own analysis code can be retrieved over HTTPS by DOI resolution. The Zenodo record is access_right open (pack).

A1_1.evidence: The protocol is open and free (HTTPS DOI resolution), and the R source code is open.

A1_2.evidence: The code is fully open and needs no authentication (pack access_right open), which satisfies A1.2 under v2.1.

A2.evidence: Zenodo deposit (platform-table Row 2): metadata always publicly accessible, and a tombstone keeps the DOI on withdrawal.

I1.evidence: The code is in R, an open, formal, and widely shared language: "The entire R code (R Core Team, 2024) used for all the analysis and visualizations" (p. 2).

I2.evidence: Searched the paper and pack for FAIR vocabularies applied to the code or its metadata (for example, CodeMeta terms or controlled subject schemes). None evidenced.

I3.evidence: Searched for PID-based, typed references from the code to its dependencies or related resources. R is cited only by URL ("R Core Team, 2024 ... http://www.R-project.org/"), no package dependencies are cited with PIDs, and the pack records no related-identifier fields.

R1.evidence: The paper describes what the code does: Bayesian Generalized Additive Models with stated families and link functions (Fig. 2 caption: zero-one inflated Beta with logit link; Gaussian with identity link; Negative Binomial with log link), Kendall's W, PCA, and Borda count. It also says "Further details about the model specifications and diagnostics are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14897252" and that all figures, tables, and test results can be reproduced from the compendium.

R1_1.evidence: The paper asserts "The R code is released under the MIT license" (p. 2), but the service records cc-by-4.0 for the same deposit (pack licence_conflicts: conflict true). The more restrictive licence governs a same-artefact disagreement. Either licence is clear and identified, so R1.1 is satisfied.

R1_2.evidence: The code has a versioned release lineage: concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14897252 resolves to version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15603267, archived from the GitHub repository benmarwick/web-of-science-archaeology (pack). The paper documents the processing pipeline the code implements, from data source to filtering to metrics to models (pp. 2-4), and names the software environment (R Core Team, 2024).

R1_3.evidence: The code is distributed as a research compendium following the R-package-based compendium convention ("code and data in this compendium (Marwick et al., 2018)", p. 2), and is described by a DataCite metadata record (pack). Both are qualifying routes for code (package structure and generic metadata schema).
